article_content: The United States has concluded that a military coup has taken place in Niger. In accordance with section 7008 of the Department of State's annual appropriations act, the U.S. is suspending most forms of assistance to the government of Niger. On August 5, the U.S. paused foreign assistance programs worth nearly $200 million, which are now officially suspended under section 7008. Furthermore, the Millennium Challenge Corporation has halted all assistance, including a $500 million Niger Regional Transportation Compact and activities tied to the 2018 Compact. Despite this, the U.S. remains committed to providing life-saving humanitarian, food, and health assistance to the Nigerien people. The U.S. will continue collaborating with regional governments to advance shared interests in West Africa. We stand in solidarity with the Nigerien people and their aspirations for democracy, prosperity, and stability. Since the coup, we have supported ECOWAS' efforts to restore democratic governance. Any resumption of U.S. assistance requires the National Council for Safeguarding the Homeland to establish democratic rule quickly. The U.S. calls for the immediate release of Mohamed Bazoum, his family, and all those detained.

I henhold til seksjon 7008 i Departementet for stats årige bevilgningsvedtak, suspenderer USA de fleste former for assistanse til Niger-regjeringen. Den 5. august pauserte USA utenlandske assistanseprogrammer verdt nesten 200 millioner dollar, som nå er offisielt suspendert i henhold til seksjon 7008. Videre har Millennium Challenge Corporation stoppet all assistanse, inkludert en 500 millioner dollar stor Niger Regional Transport Compact og aktivitetene knyttet til 2018-avtalen. Til tross for dette, forblir USA commitert til å tilby livreddende humanitær-, mat- og helseassistansk til befolkningen i Niger. USA vil fortsette å samarbeide med regionale regjeringer for å fremme felles interesser i Vest-Afrika. Vi står i solidaritet med folket i Niger og deres aspirasjoner om demokrati, velstand og stabilhet. Siden kuppet har vi støttet ECOWAS' innsats for å gjenopprette demokratisk styre. Gjenopptakelse av amerikansk assistanse krever at Nasjonalrådet for hjemlandssikkerhet etablerer demokratisk styre raskt. USA ber på nytt om øyeblikkelig frigjøring av Mohamed Bazoum, hans familie og alle som er arrestert.

article_content: South Korea has rejected a North Korean proposal to hold military talks in late May or early June, labeling the offer as a 'genuine effort to rebuild trust that lacks proper context.' A South Korea Defense Ministry spokesman argued that the North's proposal, issued Saturday, was purposefully vague on denuclearization to avoid scrutiny and instead aimed to leverage international empathy to ease sanctions and influence public opinion. The Defense Ministry maintains that North Korea is exploiting global concerns to reduce its international isolation. The Korean Peninsula remains highly tense, as the two Koreas are technically still at war following their early 1950s conflict, which ended without a formal peace treaty. Approximately 28,500 U.S. troops are stationed in South Korea as a strategic deterrent against potential threats.

article_content: Prosecutors in Peru have launched an embezzlement probe targeting presidential candidate Keiko Fujimori and her husband. The investigation into their alleged misuse of campaign funds began discreetly in March but gained public attention after a report in the Lima-based newspaper El Comercio on Friday. The probe focuses on suspicious financial transactions and unreported campaign contributions. Fujimori has denied any involvement but avoided answering specific questions. The revelation comes just two weeks before the presidential election and follows the resignation of a Fujimori aide implicated in a separate money laundering investigation. Fujimori is locked in a tight race with former World Bank economist Pedro Kuczynski. If elected, she would become Peru's first female president, though her candidacy is controversial due to her father's authoritarian regime. Alberto Fujimori, her father, is currently serving a 25-year sentence for human rights abuses and corruption. Many Peruvians remain skeptical of Keiko Fujimori, fearing a return to her father's oppressive policies.

article_content: A federal judge in Texas has surprisingly decided not to immediately dismantle the DACA program, despite earlier expectations. District Judge Andrew Hanen was anticipated to terminate the Deferred Action for Childhood Arrivals program after seven states, led by Texas, filed a lawsuit against DACA in May. His decision on Friday offers the nearly 700,000 DACA recipients a temporary reprieve, allowing them to request renewals that could extend their legal stay in the U.S. for up to two more years. DACA beneficiaries are granted protection from deportation and renewable work permits every two years. President Donald Trump announced the end of the program a year ago, urging Congress to create a replacement, but lawmakers have yet to agree on a solution. Judge Hanen suggested that the states suing over DACA should have acted sooner, when the program was first introduced by President Barack Obama six years ago. 'The egg has already been scrambled,' he wrote in his ruling. 'Trying to unscramble it now, especially with the risks involved, doesn’t make sense for the country.' Hanen also noted that ending DACA at this point could cause more harm than the states initially claimed it did. 'DACA is a widely supported program that Congress should seriously consider preserving,' he added. Hanen joins other judges in ruling that the program must continue for now, allowing renewals. However, unlike other judges, Hanen has a history of conservative rulings, notably blocking a similar program, DAPA, in 2015. He indicated that, like DAPA, he views DACA as unconstitutional. Hanen has given the seven states three weeks to appeal his decision to the conservative Fifth Circuit Court of Appeals. If the states fail to appeal or the higher court upholds Hanen’s ruling, DACA opponents may have to wait for one of several ongoing lawsuits to reach the Supreme Court. For now, the delay is positive news for DACA recipients, who will have more time to seek renewals and maintain their benefits.

Hans beslutning på fredag gir de nesten 700 000 mottakerne av DACA en midlertidig Gnist, og lar dem søke om fornyelse som kan forlenge deres lovlige opphold i USA i opptil to år til. DACA-mottakere får beskyttelse mot deportasjon og fornybare arbeidstillatelser hver to år. President Donald Trump kunngjorde året før at han ønsket å avslutte programmet, og oppfordret Kongressen til å erstatter det, men lovgivere har ennå ikke kommet til enighet om en løsning. Dommer Hanen foreslo at statene som saksøkte DACA burde ha handlet tidligere, da programmet først ble innført av president Barack Obama for seks år siden. 'Eggene er allerede slått ut,' skrev han i sin dom. 'Å prøve å sette dem tilbake i skallen nå, særlig med de risikene det medfører, er ikke meningsfylt for landet.' Hanen noterte også at å avslutte DACA på dette tidspunktet kunne skape mer skade enn det statene opprinnelig hevdet det gjorde. 'DACA er et bredt støttet program som Kongressen bør seriøst vurdere å bevare,' la han til. Hanen slutter seg til andre dommere i å beslutte at programmet må fortsette for nå, og at fornyelsene må tillates. Men, til forskjell fra andre dommere, har Hanen en konservativ dommerhistorikk, mest merkbart da han blokkerte et lignende program, DAPA, i 2015. Han indikerte at, likt DAPA, ser han på DACA som grunnlovsstridig. Hanen har gitt de syv statene tre uker til å anke hans avgjørelse til den konservative Femte Kirkelige Appellrett. For nå er forsinkelsen positive nyheter for DACA-mottakere, som vil få mer tid til å søke om fornyelse og beholde sine fordeler.

article_content: The United States expressed optimism Monday regarding the official transfer of power in Cuba from Fidel Castro to his younger brother Raul, viewing it as a potential opportunity for reform. The White House indicated that the long-standing U.S. economic embargo against Cuba's communist government might be lifted. VOA's David Gollust reports from the State Department. Bush administration officials suggested that Raul Castro may be a more pragmatic leader than his brother and a potential reformer, hinting at a possible shift in U.S. policy toward Cuba now that the younger Castro is confirmed as president. In a talk with reporters regarding Sunday's unanimous decision by Cuba's National Assembly naming Raul Castro the new chief executive, State Department Deputy Spokesman Tom Casey expressed hope that this transition could lead to positive changes. Casey mentioned that the emergence of a new leader might present opportunities for dialogue, contrasting with the previous 'Castro family dictatorship.' 'We are eager to see what differences there may be in terms of the policies that are pursued,' he noted. 'In terms of the most important policies, we are hopeful for a more collaborative approach.' There were similar optimistic comments at the White House from Press Secretary Dana Perino, who said President Bush's position on the decades-old U.S. economic embargo on Cuba is under review, with potential easing of restrictions. A commission formed by Mr. Bush issued a report two years ago offering Cuba wide-ranging U.S. economic and other assistance if it began a genuine transition from communism and set free elections. Spokesman Casey noted that Cuba has expressed interest in these terms, and preliminary negotiations are underway. The handover of power from one member of the Castro family to another is seen as a positive step toward Cuba's political future.
